feature: Merge a range into one clip, and break it apart
summary: Draw a range across a cut, right click, Merge into One Clip: the covered parts of the clips on each track become one clip that plays and sounds the same. Right click it, Break Apart, and the original clips come back whole.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The walk is merge-a-range-into-one-clip-walk.

try.do: Open a recording, trim it to 0:07 and drop a second clip right after it on V1.
Drag along the ruler from 0:05 to 0:09, right click the range, choose Merge into One Clip.
Put the playhead at 0:08 and press space: the second clip plays inside the merged one.
Press Cmd-Z: the two clips are back, meeting at 0:07.
Merge again, then drag the merged clip's left edge outward: it reveals more of the recording, like a clip trims into its file.
Right click the merged clip, choose Break Apart (or press Shift-Cmd-G).

evaluate: Does Merge into One Clip sit where you'd look for it in the range's right click menu?
Is one merged clip per track right, or would you rather have everything under the range become one clip on one track, the way Premiere nests?
Does the merged clip need to look different from an ordinary clip on the timeline, the way Final Cut marks a compound clip?
Is Break Apart the right name, or would you look for Ungroup or Unnest?
rough: No mock covers merging, so the bar looks like any clip, called Merged Clip, with nothing marking it as holding clips.
The sound under a merged clip is drawn as a plain bar with no waveform, though it plays.
A merged clip can't be moved or scaled on the canvas; it only has a place on the timeline.
A transition on a cut inside a merged clip after it is split is not drawn, and a merged clip slowed down or sped up plays no sound.
A transition on a cut exactly at the range's end is paid for from the merged clip's spare; if there is none the transition shrinks.
